review_text: Brief content visible, double tap to read full content.Full content visible, double tap to read brief content.These are classic Apple, they're like magic. Assuming you have an iPhone or Apple Watch with the Ultra Wideband hardware for "Precision Finding":1. At long distance: It gives you real-time directional information to the AirTag in two-dimensional space, you get a heading plotted out on a circle, which is where the AirTag is relative to the direction you're facing, you also get the straight line distance (in whatever measurement unit you use in iOS, feet in the U.S.), just point it ahead and walk straight to it. It works at longer distances too with the second generation, in the outdoors you can probably get up to 100 feet of tracking easily.2. At close distance: It dials in with "Precision Finding", this operates in three-dimensional space instead, as you move your phone around, above you, below you, away from you, close to you, it shows you on screen in real-time if you're getting closer, this lets you home in on precisely where the item is (on the order of inches), so you don't have to search a vague area or an approximation.3. It also has the ability to emit a chime, the sound is much louder and higher in pitch in the second generation (50% louder).The setup is easy, you pull a plastic tab (which keeps the battery circuit disconnected), the circuit completes, it emits a small chime, hold it near your iPhone and it starts pairing immediately. You can assign each AirTag a unique name and emoji to identify it. These are part of the "Find My" ecosystem so it's simple to track all of your AirTags in the "Find My" app.This is one of those things you've always wanted, where after finally getting and using them you realize three things:1. Why didn't you get them earlier?2. You don't have enough of them, you need more, in fact I ended up ordering another 4-Pack.3. These make great gifts: Perfect price range for a gift, small box to wrap, extremely useful for the recipient.My first 4-Pack was used up on the following items:💰 Wallet🔑 Home, Mailbox, Miscellaneous Keyring🔑 Car Key: I don't keep other keys on the same keyring as the car key, since excessive weight can wear the tumblers in the car's ignition cylinder.🚗 Car: 3D printed a little magnetic box for it (you can just buy one as well), and hid it inside the car, in case someone steals my car.Battery replacement was made easy to keep these working indefinitely:🔋 The stainless steel cover has a leaf spring on the back side which applies outward force on the cover keeping it in place, while pushing the cover inward to overcome the leaf spring, you rotate it left/counter-clockwise to remove the cover, right/clockwise to seal the cover. The rotation will be difficult to do if your fingers or the AirTag are oily, so make sure to wash your hands and clean the AirTags with a microfiber cloth.🔋 The battery is held in place by the speaker, which is magnetic, and happens to be placed directly center under the plastic below the battery, so it holds the battery in place to prevent you from dropping the battery accidentally, great design!🔋 Instead of an expensive proprietary battery they used a standard off-the-shelf CR2032 battery, an Amazon Basics CR2032 4-Pack is around $5, they last about a year assuming you're not constantly playing sounds through them and doing "Precision Finding" often.❌ I did have one issue that wasn't an AirTag issue but a "Find My" issue. My iPhone stopped doing "Separation Alerts" entirely (the push notifications when you leave a device or AirTag behind), it's in the "Find My" app under "Notify When Left Behind At". It wasn't working for any of my devices (like my iPads) nor AirTags. The only thing that fixed it was what I read on Reddit, on your iPhone that's supposed to receive the "Separation Alerts" (the one sharing location for "Find My"), sign out of your iCloud account then sign back in, that fixed it. I noticed other issues recently like text messages not arriving until I restarted the phone, then they would all flood in at once, I think these issues were related.
